hero.headline: A company built entirely around the part everyone else skips.
hero.subhead: Kimere is a small Italian consultancy for international students. We started in June 2026 and have no interest in pretending otherwise. What we have instead is a defined method, a scope no one else covers end to end, and a habit of telling you what we can't do before you think to ask.

genesis.heading: Nobody is responsible for the hardest part
paragraphs: Italy is one of the most wanted study destinations in Europe, and its universities genuinely want international students. Everything in between is where the system stops helping. A consulate publishes its requirements and expects them met exactly. A university closes its pre-registration window on a date it sets alone. A police headquarters counts eight working days from the moment you land, and does not care that you had a delayed flight, a document held up in translation, or no Italian.

None of these bodies is doing anything wrong. Each is doing its own job correctly, in its own language, on its own calendar. The problem is that holding the whole thing together is nobody's job — so by default it falls to a nineteen-year-old who has never seen an Italian form before, usually while they are also finding somewhere to live and sitting their first exams.

That gap isn't a market opportunity we spotted. It's the reason the company exists at all. Everything on this site — the route map, the deadlines we keep repeating, the levels of support — is built around closing it.
genesis.pullQuote: The system isn't hostile. It's simply not built for someone doing it for the first time.

method.heading: What we offer instead of a track record
method.body: We have been operating since June 2026. We put that on the record rather than bury it, and it means you can't judge us on years. So judge us on this instead — the way the work is actually run, which you can assess in full before you have paid anything.

steps.title: We diagnose before we quote
steps.body: The first call maps your citizenship, your course, your city and your calendar. Only then is it clear which level of support you need — and sometimes the honest answer is a lighter one than you came expecting.

steps.title: We plan backwards from the dates that don't move
steps.body: Universitaly windows, consular appointments, the eight-working-day filing deadline. Every plan starts at the fixed dates and works back to today, so a delay becomes visible weeks before it becomes a failure.

steps.title: We prepare each file to the standard of the office receiving it
steps.body: Not a generic checklist. Each consulate, each Questura and each municipality has its own way of wanting things, and a file that satisfies one can be turned away by another.

steps.title: We go with you where being there is the service
steps.body: Some steps can be handled remotely, and we say which. For the ones that can't — the post office counter, the fingerprinting appointment, the fiscal code — being physically present, in Italian, is the entire value.

steps.title: We stay reachable after you land
steps.body: The visa isn't the finish line. Residency registration, health cover and the housing paperwork all come afterwards, and that is where a good plan quietly falls apart if nobody is still watching.

ecosystem.heading: A coordinated group of specialists, not a call centre
ecosystem.body: Kimere is not a large firm and doesn't pretend to be one. We work as a coordinated group of independent professionals, each covering a part of the route, with one person accountable to you for all of it. It's why you never get passed between departments: there are no departments to be passed between.

nodes.body: Search support, contract review before you sign, and the lease registration your residency depends on.

team.heading: The people you'll actually deal with
team.body: A small group, deliberately. You get one point of contact from the introductory call onwards, and the others are people that contact can reach in an afternoon — not a ticket queue.

values.heading: Three commitments, and what each one costs us

items.title: Transparency about money
items.body: You get the real cost of a year in Italy — tuition, rent, health cover, the funds your consulate expects to see — before you commit to anything, including us. It costs us the clients who would rather not know until later.

items.title: Legal rigour, never shortcuts
items.body: Everything we prepare follows the immigration rules as they are published, and where a case needs a lawyer or an accountant we say so instead of improvising. We don't know a faster way around a deadline, and we wouldn't sell you one.

items.title: A journey you can actually survive
items.body: The measure of this job isn't only that the paperwork was filed on time. It's that you arrived able to think about your first exam instead of your permit. That part never appears on an invoice, and it's the part we're really selling.

limits.heading: What we don't do
items: We don't issue visas or residence permits, and we don't guarantee outcomes. Those decisions belong to the consulate and the Questura alone.
We're not a licensed estate agency. We review and register contracts; we don't hold listings or take deposits on anyone's behalf.
We don't replace a lawyer or an accountant. We point you to official sources and help you act on them.
We're not accredited by, affiliated with, or acting on behalf of any university or public body.

finalCta.heading: Meet the people behind your Italian journey
finalCta.body: Fifteen minutes, no cost, no obligation. You'll speak to someone who does this work rather than a salesperson reading from a script, and you'll get an honest read on your situation whether or not you take it any further with us.
